verdicts.rationale: Running a White test helps you determine if your standard errors are biased by heteroskedasticity and need correction.
Detecting heteroskedasticity with the Breusch-Pagan test matters because heteroskedasticity invalidates the standard error formulas of OLS.
The Breusch-Pagan test specifically checks whether the variance of the regression errors depends on the independent variables.
Heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation are the two primary violations of spherical errors in regression analysis that distort standard errors.
The Breusch-Pagan test utilizes an auxiliary regression evaluated via an LM test or an F-test to check for heteroskedasticity.
While the Breusch-Pagan test checks for non-constant error variance, the Durbin-Watson test checks for correlation between errors across time.
The White test is typically implemented by running an auxiliary regression and using an F-test (or LM test) to check the joint significance of the squared residuals.
